messages:
marie: hey — customer reported failure with request_id=abc123-987 around 2026-03-15T14:22Z, i've tried Console > Requests search and got nothing. any quick ways to hunt this down?
sam: first ask: do you have a trace_id or raw span link? if you have trace_id it's usually faster to find the request from the tracing UI and then jump to logs.
lee: CLI is fastest for me: `redwood logs search --request-id abc123-987 --since 1h` or `rwctl logs find --req abc123-987 --from 2026-03-15T14:00Z --to 2026-03-15T14:30Z` (the flags differ per deployment but pattern is the same).
marie: we only got a trace link from the customer: https://tracing.prod.redwood.com/trace/7f4b2c8e. when i paste that into Console > Traces it shows spans but no obvious request link.
sam: with a trace url you can click the top-level span then open "Associated Request" (top-right) — that links to the request entry if the span had request_id injected. if there's no associated request it's usually because the request_id header wasn't propagated into the service that produced the span.
lee: if Console link is missing, use the trace id to grep logs for the span id or trace id: `redwood logs search --query 'trace_id:7f4b2c8e' --since 1h` or `redwood logs search --query 'span_id:7f4b2c8e'`. our logging pipeline indexes trace_id and span_id fields.
jordan: short checklist i use: 1) confirm exact timestamp range 2) try `trace_id:` search 3) fallback to searching partial request_id string (some clients truncate) 4) if private deployment ask infra to check fluentd/otel exporter.
marie: tried `trace_id:` and got a couple lines from a gateway service that doesn't include request_id. how do i map from that to the downstream request?
sam: common pattern: gateway logs include incoming headers — look for `x-request-id` or `x-rw-req` in the gateway line and copy that. also check KV cache log lines: they sometimes emit `parent_request_id`.
obs-bot: automated hint: user guide -> https://intranet.redwood.com/docs/observability/hunting-by-trace shows examples for both Console and CLI.
lee: if you only have a span_id try `redwood traces get 7f4b2c8e --expand-spans` to list all spans and their `request_id` tags. sometimes the tag is named `http.request_id` or `request_id`.
marie: nice — `redwood traces get` printed a span with tag `http.request_id=abc123-9870` (note extra zero). searching that returned the logs. looks like client truncated in their email.
jordan: if logs still missing: check retention window and the customer's shard/region. for hosted requests ensure you search the same region as the trace (region toggle in the Console topbar).
sam: quick grep+jq example if you pulled raw JSON logs: ```jq 'select(.trace_id=="7f4b2c8e" and .service=="gateway")' logs.json | jq .message``` also `rg "abc123-987" logs/` works for the ad-hoc bundles.
marie: marking resolved — found mismatch in id. thank you! will ping infra to update header propagation test. :tada:
lee: awesome. quick follow-up: i'll add a tiny runbook note in the observability docs about span->request mapping edge cases.
marie: please do — saves time. :thumbsup:
